children: ASML Holding's plans to boost production of its semiconductor-making machines and remarks that some customers are expressing interest in orders for 2029 and 2030 show that demand visibility continues to improve, Citi analysts write in a note to clients. They say the debate on the Dutch stock is increasingly shifting toward the scale of expansion in 2028 and beyond and the potential boost to margins from higher prices and adoption of its higher-end machines. Finance chief Roger Dassen said ASML had now completed conversations with key customers on pricing, with effects becoming visible partly as of 2027. (mauro.orru@wsj.com)
